source_ref: https://github.com/data-liberation-project/va-ssvf-survey-data (data/raw/FINAL Data - FY 2016-2017_Excluding PII.xlsx; data/documentation/1772 VA SSVF Data Dictionary.xlsx; pdfs/VA SSVF Year End Report FY16.pdf; pdfs/VA SSVF Year End Report FY17.pdf; pdfs/Statistical Summary 1.1.2015 - 2.10.2016.pdf)
note: Item codes are bare integers the IRW processing script invents via row_number() over unique() of the pivoted column names, so the mapping was settled by RE-RUNNING that script over the FOIA source spreadsheet (data-liberation-project/va-ssvf-survey-data, data/raw/FINAL Data - FY 2016-2017_Excluding PII.xlsx) rather than inferred: after df[,-c(2:29)] and the seven named drops, 59 columns survive in the order q1..q6, q8.into, q8.1-1a/b/c, q8.2-2a/b/c, q8.3-a_1..8/b_1..8/c_1..8, q8.4-a_1..6/b_1..6/c_1..6, q15..q18, and the reproduced per-item n matches live per-item n for all 59 items with total 340,723 = 340,723. Wording: q1-q4 verbatim from the FOIA year-end reports (VA SSVF Year End Report FY16/FY17, p.1 question table); the service-grid and q15/q16 wording verbatim from the FOIA data dictionary (1772 VA SSVF Data Dictionary.xlsx), which labels the structurally identical grid of the FY2018-2020 spreadsheet; q17/q18 verbatim from the 'Statistical Summary 1.1.2015 - 2.10.2016' FOIA PDF, items 58 and 59. Direction of coding checked against published totals, not assumed: with 1=Extremely Poor..5=Excellent and the analogous ascending coding for q2/q3/q4, FY2016 gives 8,909/10,997 = 81.0% top-two against the FY16 report's 80.9%, and the reversed reading gives 13.1%; q3 correlates +0.869 with q1, so q3 runs 1=Very Dissatisfied..5=Very Satisfied, the OPPOSITE of the direction the data dictionary states for the FY2018-2020 satisfaction items. Deliberate blanks: item 7 ('Q8 into', live resp set {1}) ships no item_text and no option_text; items 43/49/55 (the sixth Other Supportive Services row, a write-in whose companion _6_TEXT columns the script drops) ship the data dictionary's block stem with no sub-service label, because the release publishes none. Rights: the FOIA-released files are US government records in the public domain per the repository README; the instrument is a VA programme satisfaction survey with no third-party rights holder, and no fee, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause was located for it.
public_note: Item 7 carries no item text: it is the FY2016-2017 form's 'Q8 into' transition column, whose only stored value is 1 and whose wording the FOIA release does not publish. Items 43, 49 and 55 are the sixth 'Other Supportive Services' row, a write-in slot whose free-text companions the IRW processing script drops, so they carry the block stem without a service label. Item 58's wording is taken from the 2015 form ('since you finished receiving services'); the neighbouring items 56 and 57 were reworded to 'since you started' by the FY2018-2020 form, so the FY2016-2017 phrasing of item 58 may differ. Note also that item 3 runs 1=Very Dissatisfied to 5=Very Satisfied (verified: r=+0.84 with the quality item 1, which runs 1=Extremely Poor to 5=Excellent), which is the reverse of the direction the VA data dictionary states for the FY2018-2020 satisfaction items.

source_ref: IRW script data/verbagg.R (item = lme4::VerbAgg$item, resp = 1 iff r2=='Y'); lme4 VerbAgg Rd; psychotools 0.7-4 VerbalAggression Rd (https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/psychotools/html/VerbalAggression.html) for the four situations; difR 5.1 verbal Rd (https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/difR/html/verbal.html) for the code-decomposition rule; edstan 1.0.6 aggression Rd + data/aggression.rda for the item sentence form and the verification counts; De Boeck & Wilson (2004) doi:10.1007/978-1-4757-3990-9 and its archived BEAR Center materials page (web.archive.org/web/20221128003829/https://old.bear.berkeley.edu/page/materials-explanatory-item-response-models); Smits, De Boeck & Vansteelandt (2004) doi:10.1002/per.529; Vansteelandt (2000) unpublished dissertation, KU Leuven
note: PASS with caveats. (1) Administered language: the 316 respondents were first-year psychology students at a university in the Dutch-speaking part of Belgium (psychotools VerbalAggression Rd, which also records trait anger as measured by the Dutch adaptation of the STAS), so the questionnaire was administered in Dutch. No Dutch wording is published in the deposit (lme4::VerbAgg ships no text at all -- its Rd documents only the factor columns) or in the book's own online materials: the archived BEAR Center page's 'Description data Explanatory Item response models.pdf' describes only the file layouts and refers item wording to the book's Table 1.1, solutions_ch1.pdf carries no items, and data.zip is not archived (404 from web.archive.org). Hence the fallback -- English in the base fields, _translated columns empty, language=Dutch. (2) text_source=translated_substitute / translation_source=third_party_english: the four situation sentences are copied verbatim from the psychotools 0.7-4 VerbalAggression Rd ('Source: Online materials accompanying De Boeck and Wilson (2004)'), cross-checked against the difR 5.1 verbal Rd and against Frontiers/PMC7307487, which is also where the item sentence form comes from ('An example item is, "A bus fails to stop for me. I would want to curse."', edstan 1.0.6 aggression Rd, same wording in PMC7307487). These three renderings differ slightly, which is why this is recorded as third-party English rather than the study's own: difR reads 'when I had used up my last 10 cents' where psychotools and PMC7307487 read 'when I used up'; PMC7307487 reads 'the clerk' where difR and psychotools read 'a clerk'. The psychotools wording ships. (3) DEVIATION, disclosed: no source I reached quotes a Do-mode item sentence. The Want-mode form is published verbatim ('I would want to curse'); 'I would curse' / 'I would scold' / 'I would shout' are its parallel construction written here, not a quoted string. difR renders the Want mode differently again ('a bus fails to stop for me. I want to shout'). (4) instructions left blank: no source reproduces the administered instructions. section_prompt carries the situation, item_text the response clause, so the published sentence is section_prompt + ' ' + item_text and no span is recorded twice. (5) option_text: the administered scale was 3-point (no / perhaps / yes), but the IRW table stores lme4's dichotomised r2 -- lme4's own Rd asserts r2 is built as levels(no, perhaps, yes) -> (N, Y, Y) and data/verbagg.R sets resp = 1 iff r2 == 'Y'. So resp 0 is 'no' and resp 1 is 'perhaps or yes'; that second label is a description of the merge, not a printed option. Confirmed against the data, not just the script: live endorsement totals equal edstan's perhaps-or-yes column exactly (3611) and not its yes-only column (1530). (6) mapping_basis=paper_explicit: the difR Rd states the decomposition rule against the same codes ('Each item name starts with S followed by a value between 1 and 4, referring to one of the situations below ... The second part of the name is either Want or Do ... The third part ... either Curse, Scold or Shout'), and lme4's own btype/situ/mode columns reproduce that decomposition for all 24 codes (situ: S1,S2=other-to-blame, S3,S4=self-to-blame, 12/12 each; mode and btype match the code token 24/24). data/verbagg.R does no renaming -- item is VerbAgg$item verbatim, including the lowercase-w 'S4wantCurse'. See verify_verbagg.R; status PARTIAL, because nothing internal to the table distinguishes bus from train or store from operator. (7) Rights: no reserved right found. No register row covers this instrument. The wording is distributed by De Boeck and Wilson's own public online materials and reproduced verbatim in two CRAN packages' documentation (difR, psychotools; GPL), and neither those pages nor the lme4 deposit state a fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term. Upstream, Ip et al. (2004) record that the situations and responses were selected from Endler & Hunt's (1968) S-R Inventory of Hostility; no rights page or quotable clause for that inventory was located either. Shipped under 'silence is permission'.
public_note: Item text is shown in English: Vansteelandt's questionnaire was administered in Dutch to Dutch-speaking Belgian students and no Dutch wording is published in the lme4 deposit or in De Boeck and Wilson's online materials, so the English rendering reproduced in the psychotools and difR package documentation ships instead, with the 'I would curse' form of the do-mode items written as the parallel of the published 'I would want to curse'; note also that resp=1 merges the administered 'perhaps' and 'yes' options because the table stores lme4's dichotomised r2
